messages:
Samantha Li: paging @oncall, OmegaCorp (dedicated VPC) is showing steady queue depth growth on their dedicated pool for the last ~6m, 99th latency spiking to ~6s and token backpressure visible in scheduler metrics. Error rate climbing to 2.9% (timeout + 502).
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: tenant=omegacorp pool=dedicated-vpc-uk-west severity=sev2 — oncall: @Rajiv Patel. See /incidents/1849501234 for details.
Rajiv Patel: grabbing this. quick look: tenant queue length per shard = [120, 95, 130, 4], one shard looks healthy, rest have large inflight and high batch sizes (~12 requests per batch, avg tokens/batch 5200). Suspect max_batch_tokens and scheduler weight mis-tuned for Omega's long-context workloads.
Maria Gomez: that matches runtime traces I saw earlier (kv cache thrash + oversized batches). For dedicated tenants we typically cap max_batch_tokens to 4096; looks like their model variant is allowing >8k because of misapplied profile during a recent rollout.
Kevin Cho: customer impact: reported slowdowns in production widgets (support ticket 98321). CS is on standby; they're getting timeouts in 15-20% of requests to the embed endpoint. Can we give ETA for mitigation?
Rajiv Patel: immediate mitigation plan: 1) force per-tenant scheduler caps (max_batch_tokens=2048, max_concurrent_requests=8) on the 3 hot shards; 2) enable tenant-specific small-model-fallback (route 30% traffic to variant:redwood-compat-medium); 3) temporarily bump shard isolation to prevent cross-tenant bursting. Doing 1 now.
ops-bot: Running config apply: `redwoodctl tenant patch omegacorp --set scheduler.max_batch_tokens=2048 --set scheduler.max_concurrent_requests=8 --shards=0,1,2` — started at 2024-11-14T09:12:10Z (async).
deploy-bot: config rollout started to dedicated-vpc-uk-west pool. Canarying to shard 0.
Rajiv Patel: canary shard 0 patched, observing metrics... batch size median dropped from ~11 to ~4, avg tokens/batch from 5200 -> ~1900. Latency p50 unchanged, p95 dropped from 2.1s -> 1.1s. Error rate on shard0 now 0.8%.
Maria Gomez: good. pushing same small change to shards 1 and 2 but will also flip the model fallback flag for traffic shaping: `redwoodctl route modify omegacorp --fallback=redwood-compat-medium --fallback-weight=0.3` (doing it now).
Kevin Cho: telling CS team to confirm if customer sees improvements. ETA for full rollout?
Rajiv Patel: shards 1 & 2 patched. Monitoring dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/observability/omegacorp/1849501234 — watch request queue and model_kv_miss. I'm going to keep a manual throttle knob open: `tenant.surge_shaper=enabled` to prevent new large batches during warmup.
incident-bot: Escalation: if error rate >3% for 10m, page senior-runtime. Current policy active: auto-fallback to compatible variants.
Maria Gomez: after full patch p95 across pool ~1.2s, error rate 0.9%, queue depth reduced by ~70%. However throughput per second dropped ~18% (expected due to smaller batch efficiency). This is acceptable as temporary mitigation; need follow-up to tune quantization/profile to get cost back.
Rajiv Patel: agree. Next actions: - schedule a 1hr postmortem with runtime+dedicated teams (do we have capacity today?) - open ticket to audit recent model-profile rollouts that removed the 4k cap - propose adding a safety gate in the control plane to prevent per-tenant max_batch_tokens > 8192 without lead approval.
Samantha Li: noted. I'll create the postmortem stub and tag runtime/dedicated. CS wants a short customer-facing blurb; Kevin can you draft a one-liner about mitigations and ETA for perf improvements?
Kevin Cho: on it. Draft: "We applied a temporary scheduler cap and a fallback model which reduced error rates and latency; we expect to restore normal throughput after tuning over the next 48h."
Rajiv Patel: handing off to next oncall @Maria Gomez for 30m watch and follow-up. If anything regresses, page escalation.
Maria Gomez: taking over. I'll keep an eye for kv cache thrash and follow up with runtime team about reintroducing a tuned batch profile (target: max_batch_tokens=3072 + quantization profile v2).
Samantha Li: thanks team :thumbsup: — closing pager for now, but not the thread. Will update the incident stub with timeline and actions.
incident-bot: Pager resolved for oncall: Rajiv Patel at 2024-11-14T09:19:14Z. Resolution summary added to /incidents/1849501234.
Maria Gomez: FYI once we have postmortem, propose a small control-plane validation rule: reject tenant configs where `scheduler.max_batch_tokens` * `avg_batch_size_est` > node_max_tokens, otherwise warn. Saves a lot of troubleshooting.
Rajiv Patel: +1 to validation rule. I'll include it in the PM notes.
Kevin Cho: CS updated customer with draft blurb; they acknowledged and asked for status emails every 12h until resolved.
Maria Gomez: Observability note: add a short-lived eval set for Omega to detect correctness regressions when we route to redwood-compat-medium. I'll spin it up after handoff.
Samantha Li: thanks all. Maria, Rajiv, Kevin, leave any follow-ups here and I'll track.
